Industrious round core rules for spare blankets
This section outlines what applies on every shift
Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: keep companion animal check-in calm, safe, and consistent for travelers and pets.

The desk team gives clear guidance, checks carrier fit, and confirms that each booking has the right paperwork before a pet moves toward boarding. Staff should stay polite and steady, since small mistakes can turn into avoidable delays. When a case needs extra review, the safety coordinator steps in to look at hazards, storage needs, and any special handling notes. The welcome team should help passengers understand the path ahead, keep the lane uncluttered, and make sure the pet stays comfortable through each handoff.

<<FACT F067>> If the carrier looks damaged, crowded, or poorly secured, the agent must pause the process and ask for a safer option before any further step. Keep water, cleaning supplies, and spare liners close to the desk, and refresh them as part of normal opening checks.

<<FACT F079>> When a traveler presents a certificate, the agent compares it with the booking notes and makes sure the details match the animal, the route, and the current trip plan. If anything is missing, the team should explain the gap in plain language and direct the traveler to the next safe step without arguing or guessing. Millie, Mei Alvarez, and Nikhil Okafor may be used in examples only when that helps with a live case.

If the issue cannot be settled at the counter, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor right away.
